_readme: The Languages of Ayuma, transcribed from DJ's family-tree chart (1765-AFA snapshot, matching config.presentYear). Modelled on a classic Indo-European tree: roots + subfamily boxes sit in antiquity, the 60 numbered tip languages are all recent, and a representative selection of flagships carry named Ancient/Classical -> Old -> Middle -> Modern stage chains (straight-down columns with clean hand-overs). NOTE: all born/died years are INVENTED placeholders (staggered, not real Andah chronology) added at DJ's request from a dateless cladogram — replace with real dates when known. Disambiguations from the chart: first "Southern Yvian" -> "Northern Yvian"; the two "Hadan" tips are ids hadan-yvian / hadan-fermere.

languages.name: Unwosian
languages.notes: Wiki (Alzuria (region)): the Kaaldari and Unwosians dominated Alzuria from the beginning of recorded history, 3100 BFA, until the Ukhdari conquests of 556 BFA; Tusil River: an Unwosian river name passed into Kaalsite. Extinct isolate and substrate. Death date a placeholder.

languages.name: Carth
languages.notes: Wiki (Emara, Elishara River): the Carth tribes lived in Emara before the Ecossian settlement; Carthic river words survive in Vestorian and Hadan. Extinct isolate and substrate. Dates are placeholders.

languages.name: Almaglean
languages.notes: Wiki (Almaglean Empire): the Later Almaglean Tribes (103 AFA) founded the empire that ruled Areoix Lie 189-522, "the first and only foreign imperial dynasty in Arten history". Placed as an isolate because it was foreign to Arten: DJ to check. Death date a placeholder.

languages.name: Seniaaii
languages.notes: Wiki (Gaeiya, Eldjo): the Seniaaii occupied Emara 1532-1556 (the Seniaaii wars). Origin not stated on the wiki, so placed as an isolate: DJ to check. Dates are placeholders.

languages.name: Tyrnotean
languages.notes: Wiki (Pelugrotoa, Inania): the Tyrnotean people are 4.2% of Pelugrotoa and 10.3% of Inania. DJ, 19 Oct 2026: its own family; spoken along the Inania border (north Pelugrotoa, south Inania) before the Pelugrotoans came, beside Kiesian to the south; not spoken in 1765, its people speaking Pelugrotoan or Inanian. Birth and death dates are placeholders (death: before the late 17th-century centralisation of Pelugrotoa).

languages.name: Biorundi
languages.notes: Wiki (Finae): one of the indigenous peoples of Finae before the Finaeans came from the Pyrru hills (7th to 9th centuries); still an ethnic group there. DJ, 19 Oct 2026: added as an isolate (family of one). Dates are placeholders.

languages.name: Trenz
languages.notes: Wiki (Finae): one of the indigenous peoples of Finae before the Finaeans came (7th to 9th centuries); still an ethnic group there. DJ, 19 Oct 2026: added as an isolate (family of one). Dates are placeholders.

languages.name: Garlls
languages.notes: Wiki (Finae): one of the indigenous peoples of Finae before the Finaeans came (7th to 9th centuries); still an ethnic group there. DJ, 19 Oct 2026: added as an isolate (family of one). Dates are placeholders.

languages.name: Etolic
languages.notes: Wiki (Jshain): Jshain has been inhabited since prehistoric times by the Etolic, before the Shrewa and the Passonians came in the 1st century. DJ, 19 Oct 2026: added as an isolate (family of one). Dates are placeholders.

languages.name: Shrewa
languages.notes: Wiki (Jshain): the Shrewa peoples arrived in the 1st century as part of the Shrewa expansion, while the Passonians settled the coast. DJ, 19 Oct 2026: added as an isolate (family of one). Dates are placeholders.

languages.name: Hepdan
languages.notes: Wiki (Galca, Isnti): the (Yaddan) Hepdan peoples migrated from the Amoray to the Galcan Peninsula in the early 5th century (the Yadification); the Hepdan Empire ruled Galca until 692. DJ, 19 Oct 2026: added as an isolate (family of one). Dates are placeholders.

languages.name: Fravalans
languages.notes: Wiki (Ilicuhe): many Fravalans-speaking peoples migrated into Ilicuhe in the 8th and 9th centuries, under the Pyrelia Kingdom. DJ, 19 Oct 2026: added as an isolate (family of one). Dates are placeholders.

languages.name: Earuhty
languages.notes: Wiki (Sunsokua, Galca): the Earuhty and Kuhn peoples came to Sunsokua in the 4th century after the Yaddan invasions of Galca. DJ, 19 Oct 2026: added as an isolate (family of one). Dates are placeholders.

languages.name: Anaspan
languages.notes: Wiki (Galca): the Anaspans were assimilated by the Dlermans and other Galcan peoples. DJ, 20 Oct 2026: added as an isolate (family of one). Dates are placeholders.

languages.name: Qutoto
languages.notes: Wiki (Etretes): among the ancient peoples of Etretes; the Qutoto were assimilated by the Aram and other peoples. DJ, 20 Oct 2026: added as an isolate (family of one). Dates are placeholders.

languages.name: Aram
languages.notes: Wiki (Etretes): the Aram assimilated the Qutoto; Etretes then took up Trian culture through the Trian Empire's conquests in the Bronze Age. DJ, 20 Oct 2026: added as an isolate (family of one). Dates are placeholders (died moved to about 1100 AFA, 21 Oct 2026: Trianised from 800 BFA where Trian came, but in the southern desert, which Trian never reached, till the Dahens came in the 10th-11th centuries)

languages.name: Yethran
languages.notes: Wiki (Estijan, Alzuria (region)): the Yethran Empire "originated from Alzuria", conquered it in the 7th century, and in 842 the Uvei adopted something from it. Placed in the Alzurian branch under Old Kaalsite: DJ to check. Dates are placeholders.

languages.name: Escaran
languages.notes: Wiki (Easuhura): the Escarans conquered Easuhura in 524; the Escaran Channel lies between Easuhura and western Emara, so placed in Saetnde, the branch of Emara: DJ to check. Dates are placeholders.
